seoTitle: How to Cancel or Retract an Offer on eBay
metaDescription: Learn how to cancel a Best Offer on eBay two different ways, deleting it from your list or formally retracting it, plus the time window eBay enforces.
intro: Accidental offers happen, and eBay gives you two different ways to walk one back. They are not the same thing. Deleting simply clears the offer off your list. Retracting is a formal withdrawal with a stated reason that eBay records against the listing, and it's only available within a specific window. This guide follows both paths from the same starting point, your Bids/Offers page, and adds the eligibility rules eBay applies before either one works.

steps.heading: Open Bids/Offers from your account menu
steps.body: On the eBay website, click your account name near the top left, where the greeting reads something like "Hi [name]!", to open the dropdown menu. Bids/Offers sits partway down the list, next to Watchlist, Purchase History, and Selling. It's the central page for anything you've bid on or offered on, split into tabs for Bidding, Best Offers, and Didn't Win. Worth bookmarking if you're active on auction-style listings regularly.

image.caption: The account dropdown from the eBay homepage. Bids/Offers is listed between Watchlist and Purchase History.

steps.heading: Find the offer in your Offers list
steps.body: Under the Best Offers tab, each offer shows its status, the item, the price you offered against the seller's asking price, and a countdown to when the offer or listing expires. Every row has a checkbox on the left, and a Delete button sits above the list next to Status and Sort filters. eBay also caps how many offers you can make on one item, generally three and five for vehicles, and expired, declined, and retracted offers all count toward that limit. Checking the box and clicking Delete is the fastest way to clear an offer that's already expired or lost.

image.caption: An offer on the Best Offers tab, with its checkbox and the Delete button above the list, plus a More actions dropdown next to Make Best offer.

steps.heading: Know what Delete really does
steps.body: Checking a box and clicking Delete removes that row from your Offers list. It's housekeeping, not a formal cancellation with the seller. It fits offers that have already expired or lost, where there's nothing left to retract. If the offer is still active and you want the seller to know it's withdrawn instead of just gone from your own list, that's a different action, covered next.

steps.heading: Open the offer's details to cancel it formally
steps.body: For an active offer you still want withdrawn, open its listing and use View offer details instead of deleting from the list. That takes you to the offer's own page, where the real retraction controls live. eBay only allows a formal retraction if 12 or more hours remain before the listing ends and you placed the offer less than an hour ago. Once the seller has accepted, declined, or countered it, retraction is off the table no matter how much time is left, and deleting the row on your end won't stop them from accepting it.

image.caption: A live offer on the Best Offers tab. View offer details opens the offer's own page, where formal cancellation is handled instead of just removing it from the list.

steps.heading: Choose a reason and cancel the offer
steps.body: Inside the offer's details, the retraction page is headed "Best Offer Cancellation: Choose Reason." A dropdown lists eBay's accepted reasons, options like "Entered wrong amount" cover a simple typo, and picking one is required before the Cancel Offer button processes the withdrawal. eBay records why the offer was pulled and notifies the seller it's no longer available to accept. If the seller doesn't respond within 24 hours, or the listing ends first, eBay cancels the offer automatically anyway.

image.caption: The Best Offer Cancellation form. A reason must be selected from the dropdown before Cancel Offer completes the withdrawal.

troubleshooting.problem: Retract offer isn't available for an offer that's still active
troubleshooting.cause: eBay only allows retraction if 12+ hours remain before the listing ends and you placed the offer under an hour ago. Once the seller accepts, declines, or counters it, the window closes regardless of time left.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Delete to clear the row from your own list. A formal retraction isn't possible once you're outside those conditions.

troubleshooting.problem: eBay won't let me submit another offer on the same item
troubleshooting.cause: eBay caps offers at three per item, five for vehicles, and expired, declined, and retracted offers all count toward that cap.
troubleshooting.fix: Check your remaining attempts on the Best Offers tab before offering again, since retracting a mistaken offer still uses one up.

troubleshooting.problem: An offer disappeared from the list without me doing anything
troubleshooting.cause: Sellers have 24 hours to respond to an offer. If they don't, or the listing ends first, eBay cancels the offer automatically.
troubleshooting.fix: Nothing to fix. Check the item's status on Bids/Offers to confirm it was cancelled and not accepted.

faq.question: What's the difference between deleting an offer and canceling it?
faq.answer: Deleting from the Offers list only removes the row from your own view. It doesn't notify the seller or stop an active offer from being accepted. Retracting through the offer's own details page, with a stated reason, formally withdraws it and eBay records that.

faq.question: Do I need a reason to cancel a Best Offer?
faq.answer: Yes. The retraction form requires picking a reason from a dropdown, such as "Entered wrong amount," before the Cancel Offer button will process it.

faq.question: Can I retract an active Best Offer any time?
faq.answer: No. eBay only allows it if 12 or more hours remain before the listing ends and you placed the offer less than an hour earlier. Once the seller has responded, that window closes regardless of the time left.

faq.question: Is there a limit on how many offers I can make on one item?
faq.answer: Yes, generally three per item and five for vehicles. Expired, declined, and retracted offers all count toward that total, so retracting a mistaken offer still uses up one of your attempts.

faq.question: Is canceling an auction bid the same process as canceling a Best Offer?
faq.answer: No. Auction bid retraction is a separate eBay process with its own rules, a typo, a changed item description, or an unreachable seller, distinct from the Best Offer flow, since bids and offers work differently on the platform.

faq.question: Can sellers cancel an offer they received?
faq.answer: Sellers have their own tools for declining or ending unwanted offers, separate from the buyer-side flow covered here.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded in July 2025. The eligibility window and offer cap were missing from the original guide entirely.
